prompt.context: Your client is a wealthy former founder and CEO of a multi-national company interested in a new investment opportunity. The National Football League (NFL) wants to expand into Mexico by establishing an expansion franchise in Mexico City. This will be the NFL's first internationally based franchise, although the NFL has recently featured some games between American-based teams in Mexico City and London. The NFL is seeking owners for the team.
prompt.question: Our client has sought our advice on whether they should pursue ownership of this new NFL expansion franchise in Mexico City. Should they invest?

clarifying_info.q: Does the client have a financial target in mind?
clarifying_info.a: The client wants a positive NPV on owning and operating the team.

clarifying_info.q: How do NFL franchise owners make money?
clarifying_info.a: Teams make money through a league-wide share of TV-contract revenues and a mix of team-specific revenue streams such as advertising, tickets, etc.

clarifying_info.q: What kind of company did the wealthy client found?
clarifying_info.a: The telecoms industry. The company has a reputation as a highly innovative company, including recent technology boosting mobile internet connections in high-density places. Although our client is no longer involved with day-to-day operations, as founder he retains a strong relationship with the company.

clarifying_info.q: Does our client have any experience with sports franchises?
clarifying_info.a: No, this would be their first foray into the sports industry.

exhibits.title: Ticket breakdown
exhibits.shows: A table showing ticket pricing by seating location in the new Mexico City stadium, including quantity of seats, price per ticket, and expected occupancy rate for each tier.

framework: Financials: Initial CapEx (team purchase price, expansion fee, stadium construction); Annual revenues (tickets, advertising, merchandise, concessions, TV contract); Annual expenses (salaries, SG&A, maintenance, travel); NPV calculation using perpetuity formula

Mexican Market for Football: Competitive substitutes (soccer, TV/movies); Government relations (public funding for stadium, mayoral support); Market research for novel product (willingness to pay, viewing preferences in-stadium vs. TV vs. mobile); Ease of doing business (construction permitting, security, infrastructure such as transportation and broadband)

Owner Considerations: Alternate investment opportunities; Time remaining in harvest period and alignment with this opportunity; Synergies with existing portfolio companies (e.g., telecoms/mobile); Expertise gap in sports ownership; Exit strategy

questions.prompt: What is the NPV of owning and operating this expansion franchise?
questions.guidance: Candidate should decompose NPV into: (1) Initial CapEx — team purchase $2.25B + expansion fee $250M + stadium/startup costs $500M = $3.0B total. (2) Annual revenues — work through each revenue driver (tickets via Exhibit 1, advertising, merchandise, concessions, TV contract) to reach $530M/year. (3) Annual costs — salaries, SG&A, maintenance, travel totaling $250M/year. (4) Annual profit = $530M - $250M = $280M. (5) Apply perpetuity with growth: NPV = (280M / [14% - 4%]) - 3.0B = 2.8B - 3.0B = -$0.2B. Candidate should flag unit awareness — some revenues are per-game (multiply by 8 home games) while TV contract is annual.

math.setup: NPV = (Annual Profit / [Hurdle Rate - Growth Rate]) - Initial CapEx. Hurdle rate = 14%, growth rate = 4%. Annual profit = Total revenues - Total costs.
steps: Ticket revenue per game (from Exhibit 1): Lower Bowl = 20,000 x $200 x 90% = $3.6M; Mezzanine = 35,000 x $100 x 80% = $2.8M; Upper-Deck = 80,000 x $50 x 75% = $3.0M; Luxury Box = 1,200 x $500 x 100% = $0.6M; Total per game = $10M
Annual ticket revenue: $10M x 8 home games = $80M
Annual revenues: Tickets $80M + Advertising $56M + Merchandise $64M + Concessions $40M + TV Contract $290M = $530M
Annual costs: Salaries $200M + SG&A $30M + Maintenance $10M + Travel $10M = $250M

questions.prompt: How could the owner drive more revenue from this asset to increase its NPV?
questions.guidance: Strong candidates go beyond squeezing existing revenue streams. Excellent candidates recognize the stadium is only used a few days per year for games, creating a large underutilized asset. Ideas should show both volume and relevance. See brainstorming section for structured answer.

brainstorming.prompt: How could the owner drive more revenue from this asset to increase its NPV?

categories.name: In-game revenue
ideas: Purchase of messages to be displayed on jumbotron screen

categories.name: New revenue streams from the stadium asset
ideas: Utilize the stadium for non-football events (concerts, soccer matches, etc.)
Host training camps for local colleges or high schools

categories.name: Change league structure
ideas: Re-negotiate the revenue sharing model with the league

recommendation: The owner should NOT invest in the football team — the NPV is -$0.2B under the base-case assumptions, which does not meet the client's goal of a positive NPV.
An alternative recommendation to invest is defensible if the candidate acknowledges the negative NPV but argues convincingly that the brainstormed revenue-enhancement ideas could close the $200M gap.
risks: Given the novelty of this opportunity, many estimates (e.g., stadium occupancy rates, advertising revenues) carry high uncertainty — the real NPV could be significantly higher or lower than modeled.
The Mexican market for American football is unproven; consumer willingness to pay and attendance may differ materially from assumptions.
Operational risks of running an international franchise with no prior sports ownership experience.
next_steps: If not investing: find an alternative investment opportunity that generates a positive NPV above the 14% hurdle rate.

If reconsidering: commission market research on Mexican consumer willingness to pay and attendance; model upside scenarios using brainstormed revenue ideas; explore synergies with the client's telecoms company (e.g., paid stadium wifi, mobile streaming deals).
